newsitem.title: USA: U.S. faults Israeli closure of Palestinian offices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. faults Israeli closure of Palestinian offices.

text.p: The United States criticised Israel on Wednesday for the second time in a week, saying a decision to shut down four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem was "very difficult to understand."

"As the President and the Secretary of State have both said, this is a time when it is very important that the (Middle East) parties take steps that will build confidence between them," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"It is therefore very difficult to understand why the Israeli government made such a decision at this time when there is a very difficult environment in the relationship with the Palestinians," he told reporters.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the closure on Tuesday. His spokesman said on Wednesday it would be impossible for Israel to carry out a West Bank pullback due this week unless the offices were shut down.
Israel says the operation of the offices violates peace agreements with the PLO under which the Palestinian Authority gained self-rule over Gaza and parts of the West Bank.
But the PLO's top official in Jerusalem charged that the decision was aimed at stirring conflict with the Palestinians.
Netanyahu's move followed his decision last week to authorise a plan to build 6,500 more Jewish homes in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.

That decision was also criticised by Washington. President Bill Clinton, at a White House meeting on Monday with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said it would foster mistrust with the Palestinians.
Netanyahu shrugged off the criticism on Tuesday, saying it was "nothing new" and he did not intend to be influenced by opposition.
Burns said later that the issue of the offices in Jerusalem was one for Israel and the Palestinians to resolve.
"We've been told by the Palestinians that they are not offices of the Palestinian Authority," he said. "It's up to the Palestinians and Israelis to work out problems like this."

"Here we have a situation where the Israelis say they're offices, the Palestinians say they're not offices. We think it's better to have private discussions on issues like this rather than public declarations because we do worry about the environment for negotiations," he added.
